title: Weather
subtitle: thick fog, heavy rain, pouring, boiling, freezing
summary: Talk about the weather with the right nouns, adjectives and word partners.

lesson.heading: Weather conditions
lesson.note: It is very common to form weather adjectives by adding -y: fog - foggy, sun - sunny.

lesson.heading: Word partners
lesson.text: Certain adjectives always go with certain weather nouns. Learn them as pairs: **thick fog** (= bad fog), **heavy rain** (= a lot of rain; the opposite is **light rain**), a **strong wind** (= a lot of wind), a **clear sky** (= no clouds).

examples.text: We had some **heavy rain** at the weekend.
There was a **strong wind** when we were on the boat.
It rained in the morning, but the **sky was clear** by lunchtime.

lesson.heading: The sun comes out
lesson.text: When the sun appears after clouds, we say it **comes out**. To make an adjective stronger we use **extremely**.

examples.text: It was very cloudy this morning, but the sun **came out** after lunch.
The wind has **blown** all the apples off the tree.

lesson.heading: Rain and storms
lesson.text: For heavy rain we often use the verb **pour**. For a short period of light or heavy rain we use the noun **shower**. A **storm** is heavy rain with strong winds.

examples.text: We had a couple of heavy **showers** this morning.

lesson.heading: Thunderstorms
lesson.text: A period of hot weather sometimes ends with a **thunderstorm**. First it becomes very **humid**, then you hear **thunder** and see **lightning**, and heavy rain follows.

examples.note: humid = the air feels very warm and wet

examples.text: We heard **thunder** and saw **lightning** during the night.
It's getting very humid. We might have a **thunderstorm** later.

lesson.heading: Temperature: from hot to cold
rows: very cold, e.g. 10 degrees below zero

left.label: cool
left.text: Slightly cold. It can be negative or pleasant.
examples: The water in the pool was lovely and **cool**.

right.label: mild
right.text: Usually positive: not as cold as usual.
examples: I don't mind wet weather if it stays quite **mild**.

lesson.text: Below zero we say the number of degrees with minus: It was minus ten degrees in New York yesterday.

exercises.prompt: Match the words to make weather phrases.
We had really thick ___ this morning, so it was hard to see the road.
exercises.explanation: We say thick fog, not ~~heavy fog~~.

exercises.statement: If it's chilly, you may want to put on a coat.
A shower is a type of wind.
exercises.explanation: A shower is a short period of rain.

exercises.statement: A mild winter means it is colder than usual.
exercises.explanation: A mild winter means it is warmer than usual.

exercises.statement: If it's humid, the air will be very dry.
exercises.explanation: If it's humid, the air will feel warm and wet.

exercises.prompt: Is each word about hot weather or cold weather?
We had a heavy ___ this morning, but it only lasted a few minutes.
exercises.explanation: A shower is a short period of rain, so it can last only a few minutes.

exercises.prompt: It was ___ with rain when we left the house.
exercises.explanation: Pour with rain = rain very heavily.

exercises.prompt: It was cloudy and grey this morning, but when the sun ___ out it was quite hot.
exercises.explanation: The sun comes out = it appears after the clouds.

exercises.prompt: What's the ___ today? It feels much colder than yesterday.
exercises.explanation: Temperature = how hot or cold it is.

exercises.prompt: It was hot sitting in the sun, but under the beach umbrella it was nice and ___.
exercises.explanation: Cool can mean slightly cold in a pleasant way.

exercises.prompt: It was minus ten ___ in New York yesterday.
exercises.explanation: We measure temperature in degrees Celsius; below zero we say minus.
